subject: Nobody drifts from God all at once
preview: Jezebel pulled a whole nation away without forcing anyone.
linkText: Who Was Jezebel in the Bible? The Queen Who Led a Nation Into Idolatry

blocks.text: Her name is still an insult three thousand years later.
Call somebody a Jezebel and everyone knows it is not a compliment.
But most people could not tell you what she actually did.
So here is what she did.
She was a Phoenician princess who married Ahab, king of Israel.
She brought Baal worship with her and made it national policy.
She fed the prophets of Baal at her own table while she hunted the prophets of the LORD.
And when Ahab wanted a vineyard that was not his, she called a fast, paid two men to lie, and had an innocent man named Naboth stoned to death.
She never had to force a nation to walk away from God.
Nobody announced they were abandoning Him.
They just started adding Baal alongside the LORD.
Until Elijah stood up and asked, "How long halt ye between two opinions?"
And the people answered him not a word.
That is the kind of influence I want you to watch for.
The most dangerous influence does not force you away from God. It makes drifting feel normal.
It usually comes through someone close to you.
It comes wrapped in something that looks harmless.
And it happens slowly, one small compromise at a time.
Jesus even brought her name up again in Revelation, rebuking a church for tolerating "that woman Jezebel."
So her story leaves you with two honest questions.
❓ Who is influencing you, and toward what?
❓ Who are you influencing, and toward what?
In the full guide I walk through her whole story from 1 Kings 16 to 2 Kings 9, including Mount Carmel, Naboth's vineyard, and the word from God that waited twenty years.
